time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame = round(t * 24); frame 0 is t = 0
pixel_units: all positions/sizes in original-resolution pixels (x right, y down)

camera.motion: static (top-down view of a whale over a sandy seabed; seabed prop at identical pixel position in frames 0 and 70; only the animated water caustics change)
camera.view: looking straight down; whale swims in a horizontal plane facing the camera, so one metres-per-pixel scale applies (2D)

objects.name: whale
objects.description: humpback-like whale, blue-grey, long pectoral fins, the only moving object; head points left
objects.reference_point_recommendation: nose_x/nose_y (rigid snout tip) for translation; the Blender origin is presumably inside the body and translates rigidly with the snout. Mask centroid (cx,cy) and bbox centre are biased by the flapping/foreshortened tail flukes and pectoral fins - do not use them for speed.
objects.motion_summary_px: rest frames 0-2 (nose x = 1117); then swims straight left (-x) at a nearly constant ~8.6 px/frame (~206 px/s) of the nose until frame 71 (nose x 517); vertical drift < 5 px. Linear fit of nose_x over frames 3-71: x = 1127.5 - 8.567*f (quadratic term ~0).

length_nose_to_fluke_tip_along_axis.note: varies with the up/down fluke stroke (tail foreshortened when flexed); frames 0-1 at rest: 2352

bbox_height_y_fin_tip_to_fin_tip.note: set by the pectoral fins (approx. flipper span), changes as fins move

body_trunk_width_y.note: max vertical body extent 10-30% of length behind the nose (fins excluded); light dorsal edge sometimes missed by the mask, true width likely ~560-620

objects.name: whale_shadow
objects.description: faint dark diagonal blur on the seabed below/left of the whale, moves with the whale

objects.name: seabed_prop
objects.description: small static cluster on the seabed upper-left of the whale: a blue rounded rock/object with a dark curved stroke and a pale slab, surrounded by 5 small green plants/sea-weed tufts
objects.note: eyeballed from a 2x crop (frames/obj_0.png), +-10 px; the whale's dorsal fin passes just right/below it late in the clip (no contact visible)

objects.name: seabed
objects.description: sandy sea floor with moving caustic light pattern, fills the frame

events.note: first nose displacement between frames 2 and 3 (frame 3 catches up 15 px, so the real start is ~frame 1-2)

events.event: tail fluke maximally flexed (shortest apparent length)
